However, once the contract is issued, the contract quantity or contract duration can only be increased up to 25 percent. Bidders are bound to accept the revised quantity or duration. For lumpsum-based service contracts, the buyer may increase the scope of work and contract value up to 25 percent with the consent of the service provider 2. Service location Aayakar Bhavan; Income Tax Office, BSNL Building; Income Tax Guest Ho s use, Seminary Hills, Nagpur Contract period One year from commencement, extendable as per GeM/bid conditions A. Definitions and Contract Framework 1. “Buyer/Department” means the Office of the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Nagpur. “Serv ice Provider” means the successful bidder awarded the contract through GeM. 2. The contract comprises the GeM bid, applicable GeM General Terms and Conditions, Service Level Agre ement, these Additional Terms and Conditions, the accepted technical proposal, the accepted financial bid, and the award/contract issued on GeM. 2A. In the event of any inconsistency, the GeM General Terms and Conditions and the applicable Service L evel Agreement shall prevail over these Additional Terms and Conditions. The bid-specific conditions shall apply to the extent that they are consistent with the prevailing GeM provisions. 3. This is a service arrangement under an employee-welfare model. Consumers shall pay the approved selling prices directly to the Service Provider. No minimum turnover, footfall, sale or revenue is guaranteed by the Department. 4. The arrangement shall not create any lease, licence, tenancy, occupancy right or interest in Departmen tal premises. The Service Provider shall vacate and hand over the premises and assets upon expiry or ter mination. B. Duration, Commencement and Termination 5. The initial contract period shall be one year from the date specified in the GeM contract or written com mencement order. Extension, if any, shall be subject to satisfactory performance, mutual consent, compet ent-authority approval and applicable GeM provisions; it shall not be claimed as a right. 6. The Service Provider shall commence operations within the period specified in the bid/commencement order after completing verification, licence and deployment formalities. 7. Either party may terminate the contract by giving two months’ written notice, subject to GeM terms. Th e Department may terminate the contract earlier for material breach, food-safety risk, misconduct, repeat ed default, fraudulent documentation, unauthorized subletting, abandonment, insolvency or conduct preju dicial to security or reputation, after following the procedure required under applicable terms. 8. On expiry or termination, all dues, inventory, Departmental assets and premises shall be reconciled and handed over within the time directed by the Department. C. Locations, Timings and Eligible Consumers Location Service timing Operating days All days, including holid Income Tax Guest House, Seminary Hills 07:00 AM–11:00 PM ays Departmental working d Aayakar Bhavan Canteen 09:30 AM–06:00 PM ays Departmental working d Income Tax Office, BSNL Building 09:30 AM–06:00 PM ays 9. The timings specified in the location table may be reasonably modified by the Dep artment through written directions based on office requirements. This contract does

not cover special catering for meetings, conferences, functions or other separately re quisitioned events; any such requirement shall be dealt with independently in accord ance with the applicable procedure. 10. Service shall be restricted to Departmental officers/officials, authorized visitors, guests staying in the Guest House, residents of the Income Tax Colony, and their eligible family members, unless otherwise app roved in writing. D. Mandatory Menu, Portion Sizes and Service Standards 11. The following items constitute the Mandatory Fixed Menu Basket. Quoted rates shall be for the comple te prescribed unit/portion and shall include all inputs, preparation, service, overheads and applicable taxes /charges. Sl. Reasonable substitution of the seasonal vegetable may be ma de according to availability, but paneer, mushroom, baby corn and other premium items are not included i n the mandatory thali and may be offered separately as optional/additional items. 13. The Department may prescribe serving utensils or sample portion measures. Short serving, dilution, m aterial substitution or reduction below the stated minimum quantity shall constitute non-compliance. 14. In addition to the Mandatory Fixed Menu Basket, the Service Provider shall be free to prepare and sell other vegetarian food, snack and beverage items based on consumer demand, subject to the food-safety, hygiene, statutory, security and operational conditions of the contract. The description, portion size and sel ling price of such optional/additional items shall be determined by the Service Provider based on market c onditions, demand and supply and shall not require prior approval of the Department. 14A. Optional/additional items and their rates shall not be considered for technical qualification, financial evaluation or selection of the successful bidder. Their current prices shall be prominently displayed before sale and applied uniformly to consumers. No optional item shall be represented as a mandatory item or m ade a compulsory condition for purchasing a mandatory item. 14B. The Department shall not ordinarily regulate or approve the prices of optional/additional items. It ma y, however, prohibit or direct discontinuation of an optional item on grounds of food safety, hygiene, securi ty, statutory non-compliance, misuse of Departmental premises or material interference with delivery of th e mandatory services. F. Financial Bid and QCBS Evaluation 17. Each bidder shall quote a separate, unconditional, positive consumer selling rate for every item in the Mandatory Fixed Menu Basket in Part Q. Rates shall be expresse d in Indian rupees to a maximum of two decimal places and shall include all costs, ch arges and applicable taxes. A missing, conditional, nil/zero or complimentary entry s hall render the financial bid non-responsive, subject to applicable GeM provisions. Ev ery item must be supplied at its own quoted selling rate without compulsory purchas e of any other item. Sl. 3 chapatis (25–30 g flour eac h); 200 g cooked rice; 150 m Standard Vegetarian Lunch l yellow dal; 150 g seasonal To be quoted in Part Q 3 Thali vegetable curry; 50 g green salad To be quoted in Part Q 4 Tea 1 cup; minimum 120 ml 18. Evaluated Unit Basket Price (Pᵢ) = Samosa rate + Poha rate + Standard Vegetaria n Lunch Thali rate + Tea rate. Each rate relates to one complete prescribed unit/porti on. Optional items and additional servings shall be excluded from evaluation. 18A. A common evaluation multiplying factor of 1,00,000 shall apply uniformly to all bidders. The amount t o be entered in the designated GeM financial quotation field shall be: GeM Financial Quotation (Qᵢ) = Pᵢ × 1 ,00,000. This factor shall be applied once only; no further multiplication by the number of locations, servic e days, months or contract period shall be made in this calculation. 18B. The bidder shall complete and sign Part Q and upload it with the Financial Bid. The individual rates, th eir sum and the multiplied quotation shall be arithmetically consistent. A mismatch between the amount e ntered on GeM and Part Q shall be dealt with strictly under applicable GeM provisions on clarification, corr ection and responsiveness. No bidder shall be permitted to revise its commercial offer through clarification ; where correction is not permitted, a material inconsistency shall render the bid non-responsive. 18C. The factor of 1,00,000 is solely a common financial-evaluation multiplier. It is not an order for 1,00,00 0 baskets or units of any item, an estimate or assurance of actual sales, a minimum purchase commitmen t, or an amount payable by the Department. Consumers shall pay the accepted item-wise rates only for qu antities actually purchased. The Department does not undertake to pay the scaled financial quotation or a ny shortfall in sales or revenue. 18D. Illustration only: if the four rates are ₹15, ₹25, ₹100 and ₹10, Pᵢ is ₹150 and Qᵢ is ₹1,50,00,000. The re spective consumer selling rates remain ₹15, ₹25, ₹100 and ₹10. These illustrative figures are not prescrib ed prices or price ceilings. 18E. The GeM Financial Quotation is distinct from the realistically assessed estimated value of the service arrangement. EMD, performance security, applicable charges and other value-linked requirements shall be governed by the applicable GeM provisions and the published portal settings. Nothing in these conditions g rants an exemption from those provisions or authorizes alteration of the portal-generated contract outside the permitted process. 19. Among technically qualified and financially responsive bidders, the lowest GeM Fi nancial Quotation shall be Qₗ. That bidder shall receive a Financial Score of 100. For e very other such bidder: FSᵢ = 100 × (Qₗ ÷ Qᵢ). Applying the same multiplier to every b idder preserves both the price ranking and the Financial Scores. 20. The QCBS weightage shall be Technical 30% and Financial 70%. Combined Score (CSᵢ) = (TSᵢ × 0.30) + (FSᵢ × 0.70). 21. The technically qualified and financially responsive bidder obtaining the highest C ombined Score shall be ranked H-1 and considered for award, subject to applicable G eM provisions, purchase-preference requirements and verification. Since every techni cally qualified bidder receives a Technical Score of 100, the lowest GeM Financial Qu otation (equivalently, the lowest Evaluated Unit Basket Price) produces the highest C ombined Score. References to H-1 in these conditions denote the highest QCBS score ; L-1 denotes the lowest financial quotation. 22. Ties shall be resolved through the tie-breaking mechanism available under GeM or, if GeM requires the Buyer to specify a method, by the method disclosed in the bid before submission. 22A. A quotation may be examined as apparently unworkable or unbalanced where t he unscaled unit basket price or individual mandatory-item rates appear insufficient t o meet the prescribed portions, food quality, manpower, statutory and service obligat

ions, or where the distribution of prices may impair reliable performance. The multipli ed figure shall not be treated as actual revenue when examining viability. 22B. To the extent permitted by prevailing GeM provisions and functionality, the Buy er may seek a written price justification from the bidder under consideration for awar d. This may include item-wise cost build-up, input quantities and rates, recent purcha se invoices, labour and statutory costs, overheads, realistic sales/footfall assumption s and any lawful revenue support from optional-item sales or other disclosed sources. Such support shall not excuse a missing or zero mandatory-item rate, conditional sal e, reduced portion or statutory default. No assumed minimum sales shall bind the De partment. 22C. The Buyer shall record whether the explanation reasonably demonstrates sustainable performance a t the quoted prices. If the explanation is unacceptable, action including disqualification and recalculation of ranking may be taken only where permitted by the prevailing GeM provisions and portal functionality. Mer e comparison with another bidder's rate or a subjective view that a rate is low shall not, by itself, be suffici ent. G. Rates, Display, Billing and Revision 23. The accepted individual selling rates recorded in Part Q, subject only to a revision permitted under Clauses 25B to 25D, shall be the approved consumer rates for the fo ur mandatory items. These rates and prescribed portions shall be prominently displa yed at every location. The scaled GeM quotation shall not be displayed or charged as a consumer price. Optional items and current prices shall be displayed separately. N o amount above the applicable displayed price or compulsory add-on shall be charge d. 24. Payment for routine food sales shall be directly between the consumer and the S ervice Provider at the approved item-wise rates for actual quantities purchased. No p eriodic, lump-sum or minimum payment by the Department arises from the scaled ev aluation quotation. The Department shall not be responsible for individual unpaid bill s or guarantee any minimum consumption. Separately requisitioned event catering is outside this contract under Clause 9. 25. Approved mandatory-item rates shall ordinarily remain firm during the initial contract period of one ye ar, subject only to the Exceptional Price Review mechanism in Clause 25B. No routine, retrospective or unil ateral escalation shall be admissible. 25A. Rates of optional/additional items may be fixed and revised by the Service Provider based on deman d, supply and market conditions without prior Departmental approval, provided the current price is promin ently displayed before it becomes effective. The Department shall be concerned with approval and revision only of the four Mandatory Fixed Menu item prices. 25B. After expiry of six months from commencement, the Service Provider may seek one Exceptional Price Review during the initial term where it demonstrates an overall increase of at least 10% in the cost of the principal inputs required for the Mandatory Fixed Menu Basket compared with the corresponding costs pre vailing in the month of bid submission. The request shall include base-period and current purchase invoice s, commercial LPG costs, applicable statutory wage/tax changes, item-wise cost calculations and the exact revision sought. 25C. A committee may examine the request with reference to documentary evidence, prevailing local ma rket prices, relevant official price indices and the welfare nature of the canteen. Any revision shall not be a utomatic or claimable as a right; shall require competent-authority approval and permissibility under GeM; shall operate prospectively from written approval; and shall be limited to the lower of the verified cost incr ease or 10% of the existing approved mandatory-item prices. As far as practicable, an approved revision s hall be applied as a common percentage to all four mandatory prices. 25D. For an approved extension beyond the initial term, mandatory-item prices may be reviewed before c ommencement of the extension on a written, evidence-based proposal. Revised rates shall require compet ent-authority approval, mutual acceptance and incorporation in the extension in accordance with GeM. If t he applicable GeM functionality does not permit the proposed revision, no off-portal price amendment shal l be made.

25E. Submission or rejection of a price-review request shall not entitle the Service Provider to increase pri ces, reduce portions or quality, suspend or abandon services. If continuation is commercially unacceptable , the Service Provider may invoke the contractual termination provision and shall maintain services during the prescribed notice period, without prejudice to the Department's rights and alternative arrangements. 26. The Service Provider shall provide UPI and such other digital-payment facilities as may reasonably be directed. Where GST or any other tax is applicable, the Service Provider shall issue a compliant invoice/rec eipt and maintain the records required under law. 26A. No tip, donation, service charge or other voluntary or compulsory payment shall be solicited from co nsumers. H. Food Quality, Hygiene and Safety 27. Only fresh, wholesome and hygienically prepared food made from good-quality ingredients shall be se rved. Re-use of stale food, adulterated material, expired ingredients or cooking oil beyond permissible foo d-safety limits is prohibited. 28. The kitchen, pantry, dining area, counters, storage areas, utensils, crockery, equipment and waste con tainers shall be cleaned and maintained in hygienic condition. Food shall remain covered and protected fro m contamination, pests and dust. 29. Only potable water conforming to applicable food-safety standards shall be used for cooking, beverages and serving. Where an RO/filtration facility is provided or prescribed, it shall be properly operat ed and maintained. Raw and cooked food shall be stored separately at safe temperatures. Cleaning, pest-c ontrol and food-safety records shall be maintained when required. 30. Only commercial LPG cylinders and approved cooking equipment shall be used. Domestic LPG cylinder s, unsafe connections and unauthorized high-load electrical cooking appliances are prohibited. A register o f commercial LPG cylinders received, connected, replaced and returned shall be maintained and produced during inspection. Fire extinguishers and first-aid boxes shall be provided by the Department. The Service Provider shall keep access to them unobstructed, shall not misuse or remove them and shall promptly rep ort any apparent defect or depletion to the designated officer. 31. Smoking, tobacco, alcohol, intoxicants, pets and unauthorized persons are prohibited in food-preparati on and service areas. I. Statutory Licences, Labour and Personnel 32. The canteen operator is a Food Business Operator and shall hold or obtain, before commencement, th e applicable FSSAI registration/licence for catering/canteen operations and for each premise where separat ely required. The bidder shall upload its existing valid FSSAI registration/licence, if already held, or an und ertaking to obtain the applicable registration/licence before commencement. No food service shall begin or continue without the legally required FSSAI authorization. Other registrations, labour-law permissions and i nsurance applicable to the services shall also be maintained. 33. All deployed personnel shall be at least 18 years old, trained, courteous, medically fit and properly uni formed. They shall wear clean uniforms distinct from Departmental uniforms, identity cards, aprons, hair r estraints/caps, gloves where appropriate and other hygiene gear suited to their duties. 34. Identity/address proof, recent photograph, police verification where required, and medical-fitness/com municable-disease clearance of deployed personnel shall be submitted before deployment and updated u pon replacement. Any person directed to be removed for recorded security, misconduct, hygiene or persis tent performance reasons shall be replaced within 24 hours or before the next scheduled shift, whichever i s earlier. 35. The Service Provider shall be the sole employer of its personnel and shall comply with applicable wage s, working hours, EPF, ESIC, leave, contract-labour, safety and other statutory obligations. No personnel sh all acquire any claim to Departmental employment. 35A. The Service Provider shall deploy sufficient trained manpower at each location and during each shift to ensure uninterrupted preparation, service and cleaning. Before commencement it shall submit a locatio n-wise and shift-wise deployment plan. At no time shall a food-preparation location operate without at leas t one trained cook and one helper, and each operational serving counter shall have at least one service pe

rson. Necessary relievers and additional personnel shall be deployed to comply with working-hour and wee kly-rest requirements. 36. The Service Provider shall indemnify the Department against claims, injury, accident, food-safety incid ent, labour dispute, statutory default, negligence, infringement or breach attributable to the Service Provid er or its personnel. J. Infrastructure, Assets and Utilities 37. The Department may provide identified premises, basic furniture/equipment, water and electricity as r ecorded in a jointly signed inventory. A joint inspection and inventory shall be prepared and signed at com mencement and again upon expiry or termination. Any shortage or damage beyond normal wear and tear shall be recoverable after assessment and opportunity to explain. Provision of utilities shall not authorize wasteful or unauthorized use. 38. Cooking equipment, utensils, crockery, consumables, raw materials, cleaning material and manpower shall be arranged by the Service Provider unless specifically listed as Department-provided assets. 39. The Service Provider shall not make structural alterations, install equipment, connect loads, display ad vertisements or use the premises for any purpose other than the contract without prior written permission. Personal belongings shall be kept only in the designated area. No unrelated commercial goods, domestic a rticles, hazardous material or stock unconnected with canteen services shall be stored in Departmental pr emises. 40. Loss or damage beyond normal wear and tear shall be repaired or recovered from the Service Provider after assessment and opportunity to explain. K. Inspection, Records and Performance Monitoring 41. The Department or its authorized committee may inspect food, raw materials, portions, records, kitche n, service areas, personnel and licences, including through surprise inspections. Food samples may be tak en and sent to an FSSAI-notified or NABL-accredited laboratory, as applicable. If a sample fails the prescrib ed standard, the sampling and testing cost shall be borne by the Service Provider, without prejudice to pe nalty or other action. 42. A Complaint and Feedback Register, daily menu/availability record, cleaning register and penalty/rectif ication record shall be maintained at the prescribed location and produced on demand. The daily menu, av ailability, prescribed portion and applicable price of every Mandatory Fixed Menu item shall be prominentl y displayed; optional items and their current prices shall be displayed separately. 43. The Service Provider shall immediately report any suspected food poisoning, fire, accident, gas leak, c ommunicable disease or other safety incident and cooperate with corrective action and investigation. The Departme nt may require removal of any person for recorded security, conduct or performance reasons; suitable repl acement shall be provided promptly. 47. Information concerning guests, officers, official activity, security arrangements or records observed du ring service shall be kept confidential and shall not be photographed, copied, disclosed or posted on social media. 48. No part of the contract shall be assigned, transferred, sublet or outsourced without prior written permi ssion and compliance with GeM conditions. N. Waste Management and Sustainability 49. Wet and dry waste shall be segregated and disposed of daily in accordance with municipal and Depart mental directions. Used cooking oil shall be disposed of only through an authorized channel where applica ble. 50. Single-use plastic shall be avoided/prohibited to the extent directed by law or the Department. Reusab le or environmentally preferable serving material shall be used wherever practicable. O. Dispute Resolution and Jurisdiction 51. Any dispute or difference arising out of or in connection with the bid or the contract shall, in the first in stance, be submitted in writing to the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Nagpur, or an officer/co mmittee authorized by him/her, for administrative examination and an attempt at amicable resolution. 52. If the dispute is not resolved amicably within the period prescribed under the prevailing GeM General T

erms and Conditions, it shall be dealt with strictly in accordance with the dispute-resolution and arbitration mechanism prescribed under the prevailing GeM General Terms and Conditions and the Arbitration and Co nciliation Act, 1996, as amended from time to time. 52A. Subject to the aforesaid dispute-resolution mechanism, the competent courts at Nagpur shall have e xclusive territorial jurisdiction, Nagpur being the registered address/principal place of business of the Buye r for this contract. 52B. GeM shall not be made a party to any dispute between the Buyer and the Service Provider, except to the extent otherwise required under the prevailing GeM provisions or applicable law. In the event of any in consistency between this clause and the prevailing GeM General Terms and Conditions, the GeM General T erms and Conditions shall prevail. P.
